note: HTTP Digest (RFC 2617/7616), MD5, qop=auth. Server realm "Parity", server nonce pinned to deadbeef*4 on both sides so the challenge is reproducible. Authorization headers were generated by cases/generate-digest.js. Challenge nonces are normalised to <NONCE> before comparison.

Digest username="alice", realm="Parity", nonce="deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef", uri="/digest", qop=auth, nc=00000001, cnonce="0a4f113b", response="36e68c5a936f866c866655d6ada481bf"

cases.note: control for digest-uri-replayed-at-other-path: correctly bound uri, both must accept

headers.authorization: Digest username="alice", realm="Wrong", nonce="deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef", uri="/digest", qop=auth, nc=00000001, cnonce="0a4f113b", response="33a51fdc6384c2f5fedd1bf02938202a"

cases.deviation: The port is deliberately stricter than upstream: it derives HA1 from its OWN configured realm, so a response computed under a client-chosen realm="Wrong" is rejected (401). Upstream derives HA1 from creds.realm (the client's value) and therefore authenticates. Matching upstream would mean trusting an attacker-chosen realm, weakening the port, so this divergence is kept. See passport/API-DEVIATIONS.md.
cases.note: SECURITY: response computed under a client-chosen realm. Upstream derives HA1 from creds.realm and therefore ACCEPTS; the port derives HA1 from its own configured realm and rejects. The port is the stricter of the two here.
